title: Evals
heading: Evals

verdict.heading: The assistant's guardrails, tested on every build
verdict.allPass: This suite passes {rate}, which on its own proves nothing — code that fails its tests never ships. What proves something is switching each guardrail off and counting what breaks. That's below.
verdict.someFail: {failed} of {total} cases fail in this build. Code in this state should not ship; the failing cases are marked below.

model: No model decides what gets refused. A model can only write answers, and every answer passes a number-and-source check before anyone sees it. When the model changes, these cases are how you know the guardrails still hold.

mutation.heading: Mutation testing: switch a guardrail off, count what breaks
mutation.intro: Mutation testing means breaking the code on purpose and rerunning the tests. If nothing fails, the tests were never really checking that part. Every build of this page switches off each guardrail below, one at a time, and runs every test question against the broken version.
mutation.missed: Not caught. No test checks this guardrail.

labels.category-off:ipo: Rules for IPO and listing questions
labels.category-off:future-timing: Rules for future dates and plans
labels.category-off:valuation: Rules for valuation and share price
labels.category-off:comparison: Rules for comparisons with other investments
labels.normalise-off: Clean-up of disguised spelling: look-alike letters, spaced-out letters, digits for letters, typos
labels.postcheck-off: The number-and-source check on every answer

refusals.heading: What gets refused, and why
refusals.intro: Each kind of question below is refused before any model sees it. The reason shown is the one the assistant gives, word for word.
refusals.expected: Expected outcome: refused, and handed to EnergyX Investor Relations.

adversarial.heading: Attempts to get around the refusals
adversarial.intro: People will try to slip a forbidden question past the check. Each technique below has its own tests.

obfuscation.name: Disguised spelling
obfuscation.attempts: Hides a forbidden word with dots, spaces, look-alike letters from other alphabets, invisible characters, digits or typos.

framing.name: Hypothetical or indirect framing
framing.attempts: Wraps the question in a hypothetical, a school project, a poem, a friend, or a promise that it isn't advice.

override.name: Instruction override
override.attempts: Tells the assistant to ignore its rules or pretend to be a financial adviser.

compound.name: Compound question
compound.attempts: Hides a forbidden question behind an answerable one in the same message.

language.name: Other languages
language.attempts: Asks in Spanish, German or Japanese, hoping English-only rules miss it.

emoji.name: Emoji
emoji.attempts: Asks about returns with a chart emoji instead of words.

mustNotRefuse.heading: Questions it must not refuse
body: A gate that refuses every question passes every refusal test on this page. It would also be useless.
These tests are what stop that: ordinary questions that sound risky, such as gold standard, appreciate, protected area, which must still get through. This is the part most test suites miss.
mustNotRefuse.proof: The mutation test above shows it. Switched to refuse everything, the gate still passes every refusal test, and fails {count} of these {total}.

modelSlot.heading: If the model misbehaves
modelSlot.intro: A model is only ever allowed to write the wording of an answer. These tests stand in a deliberately broken model and check that nothing it gets wrong reaches the reader.

stubs.invents-number: Invents a number that is not in the registry
stubs.number-in-words: Writes an untraced number in words
stubs.cites-unretrieved: Cites a fact it was not given
stubs.no-citations: Gives an answer with no sources

modelSlot.expected: Expected outcome: the answer is dropped and the reader sees that there is no sourced answer.

other.heading: Questions it should answer, or decline to guess
other.intro: The rest of the suite: questions the registry can answer, with the exact facts expected, and questions it can't, where the right answer is to say so.
